title: Forward coefficient comparisons by closed and geometric adjunctions
statement: Use the categories and evaluation data of [def-sfb-free-parameter-evaluation-data]. For any morphism $\varphi:R\to S$ of commutative condensed rings, use the scalar adjunction $E=S\otimes_R^L-\dashv r=D\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ from [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Its derived tensorator is induced by the scalar-unit normalized monoidal structure of [lem-sfb-internal-extension-monoidal] and preservation of flat modules [lem-sfb-internal-extension-preserves-flat], with no exactness assumption on extension. Define $g_P:EA_P[0]\to S[h_P][0]$ as the scalar transpose of the ordinary free-generator map $[t]\mapsto[t]$. It is an isomorphism: the flat free modules in [def-sfb-free-parameter-degree-zero-data] are K-flat in degree zero, and scalar extension there computes the usual free module. Given $n:N\to rN'$, define $e:R\mathcal Hom_R(A_P,N)\to rR\mathcal Hom_S(S[h_P],N')$ by scalar transposition of the closed transpose of $(g_P^{-1}\otimes1);\mu_E;E(\mathrm{ev});n^\sharp$. Define $a=p_X^*e$ followed by the canonical action identification $p_X^*r\cong r_Xp_X^*$. For any geometric $f:Y\to X$, define $t:E_Yf_R^*\to f_S^*E_X$ by scalar transposition of $f_R^*\eta_X$ followed by the inverse of the exact restriction/pullback action identification; this canonical $t$ is invertible, as computed by the balanced comparison on K-flat representatives. Define $b:R\rho_{R*}p_U^*N\to r_XR\rho_{S*}p_U^*N'$ by scalar transposition and projection transposition of $t^{-1};E_U(\epsilon_\rho);(p_U^*n;\mathrm{action})^\sharp$. These formulas define the forward maps without inverting any reverse direct-image comparison or assuming flatness of $\varphi$.

proof.text: Construct the ordinary free scalar isomorphism by uniqueness of left adjoints: free_R followed by scalar extension and free_S are left adjoint to the same underlying condensed-set functor. Applying the composite adjunction to its forward map gives the S-free-generator unit, hence its scalar transpose is precisely freeGeneratorScalar.

Compute the derived scalar adjunction unit against its universal left-derived counit, using the derived adjunction factorization and exact scalar restriction. On a single complex, the termwise ordinary unit and single-object comparisons give the same composite. Thus the counit followed by the single-complex comparison and the ordinary free scalar isomorphism is exactly freeScalarMap. The free parameter is flat, so its single complex is K-flat and that counit is invertible; all three factors are isomorphisms.

Use internal_pull_normalization_exists to obtain a universally normalized scalar/geometric isomorphism. The normalized_inverse theorem identifies its inverse with the inverse scalar mate of normalizationRestrictionPull. Whisker the exact geometric derived-functor comparisons to identify this mate with the mate of derivedComapUpperStarIso.inv. Cancel these invertible whiskered components to prove that scalarPullComparison is invertible. Define this comparison directly as the inverse-mate component. The mate unit identity shows this is exactly the scalar transpose of geometric pullback of the scalar unit followed by the restriction/pullback identification; hence its mathematical normalization is unchanged. The two consumers that unfolded the former adjunct formula are adapted to this definition.

Retain the given constructions of scalarTensor, scalarHomPoint, scalarHomMap and scalarPushMap. Their required inverses now use the two proved invertibility instances. The tensorator still uses ordinary scalar monoidality and preservation of flat objects, without assuming scalar extension exact.

proof_origin.place: Stacks Tags 07A6 and 0D6D: reuse the universal K-flat normalized comparison and its scalar-mate identification. Exact pullback derived comparisons transport it to the inverse mate of the exact restriction/pullback identification. The mate unit identity identifies this with the scalar-unit transpose. The existing free-generator proof is retained.
